class="Figure-credit"><p>Brian Jackson/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/05/21/broadview-ice-protest-grand-jury-transcript-kat-abughazaleh-trump" target="_blank" >case collapsed</a> May 21<b> </b>after Perry discovered alleged misconduct<b> </b>by the onetime lead prosecutor in the case, Sheri<b> </b>Mecklenburg.</p><p>Hogan, a veteran federal prosecutor in Chicago, took over the "Broadview Six" case after Mecklenburg withdrew from it in February. Mecklenburg allegedly committed misconduct while seeking an indictment from a grand jury — including speaking to grand jurors outside the grand jury room. </p><p>But her alleged wrongdoing had also been redacted out of transcripts given to the judge in April — a fact that Perry<b> </b>has said<b> </b>she found "most problematic."</p><p>Hogan<b> </b>has taken responsibility for redacting them. He did so the day the case collapsed.</p><p>Hogan is no stranger to controversy. In fact, claims of misdeeds during the prosecution of El Rukn street gang cases in the 1980s and 1990s led to Hogan's firing<b> </b>in 1996. He was rehired after an administrative judge cleared him of wrongdoing, according to previous reports in the Chicago Sun-Times.</p><p>He's continued to work as a prosecutor at the Dirksen Federal Courthouse, even as Boutros' office grappled with a credibility crisis created by the "Broadview Six" scandal. </p><p>Perry <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/01/broadview-six-perry-boutros-mecklenburg" target="_blank" >concluded<b> </b>last month</a><b> </b>that further “under oath”<b> </b>fact-finding was needed<b> </b>in the case. She told lawyers Oct. 1 that, “my sole focus, at this point, is on lack of candor, concealment of material facts, or other misconduct that occurred before me.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/06/27/broadview-six-boutros-chicago" >What to know about the ‘Broadview Six’ scandal rocking Chicago’s federal courthouse</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>Days later, she<b> </b>asked<b> </b>Boutros’ office to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/09/feds-appear-to-hide-name-of-government-lawyer-in-new-broadview-six-court-filing" target="_blank" >provide records</a><b> </b>that could shed light on whether the feds were telling the truth when they made specific claims<b> </b>in the case last spring. She asked the feds to turn the records over by Oct. 30.</p><p>Instead, Associate Attorney General Stanley<b> </b>Woodward, the third-highest ranking official<b> </b>in the Justice Department, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/10/30/controversial-doj-boss-takes-reins-in-tainted-broadview-6-case-stymies-judges-inquiry" target="_blank" >inserted himself into the case</a> that day. He<b> </b>asked<b> </b>Perry<b> </b>to clarify the point of her inquiry and<b> </b>told<b> </b>her<b> </b>she<b> </b>should<b> </b>make clear if her<b> </b>“request”<b> </b>for documents<b> </b>was really a “directive.”</p><p>Woodward<b> </b>also<b> </b>warned<b> </b>her<b> </b>that<b> </b>“the United States has not agreed to provide any information”<b> </b>she’d sought.</p><p>Perry<b> </b>responded<b> </b>with a seven-page<b> </b>order<b> </b>that made clear she wasn’t pleased with Woodward. She complained that the timing of his filing “could easily lead one to conclude that the goal of the filing was not to cure genuine confusion … but instead to inject unnecessary delay into these proceedings.”</p><p>However,<b> </b>she<b> </b>has now given<b> </b>the feds<b> </b>until<b> </b>Monday<b> </b>to turn over the records.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-e10000" name="module-e10000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3><b>How the “Broadview Six” case collapsed and created a credibility crisis</b></h3><br><b>April 7, 2025: </b>Andrew Boutros, a former rank-and-file federal prosecutor<b> </b>in Chicago, is appointed on a temporary basis to act as the city’s U.S. Attorney. The four-month appointment<b> </b>is made by then-Attorney General Pam Bondi.<br><br><b>July 24, 2025: </b>With Bondi’s temporary appointment set to expire, Chicago’s federal judges choose Boutros to continue as U.S. Attorney on a more permanent basis.<br><br><b>Oct. 23, 2025: </b>Boutros’ office<b> </b>secures<b> </b>a conspiracy<b> </b>indictment<b> </b>against a group of Operation Midway Blitz protesters who would come to be known as the “Broadview Six.” Most of the six defendants<b> </b>are<b> </b>involved in local Democratic politics, raising questions about selective prosecution.<br><br><b>April 7: </b>In an interview published to mark his first year in office, Boutros denies that politics<b> </b>played any role in his office’s charging decisions: “[There is] not a single case, OK, involving politics in our decision-making. Full stop. Period. Zero. And anyone who says otherwise is misstating reality. And anyone who says otherwise is an armchair expert who doesn’t know what they’re talking about. Period.”<br><br><b>April 29: </b>Boutros’ office<b> </b>drops<b> </b>the<b> </b>conspiracy<b> </b>indictment<b> </b>in the “Broadview Six” case and<b> </b>says it will move forward with misdemeanor charges<b> </b>against<b> </b>four<b> </b>remaining<b> </b>defendants. The move sparks suspicion among defense attorneys because<b> </b>prosecutors<b> </b>had been asked to give U.S. District Judge April Perry<b> </b>unredacted<b> </b>transcripts of the grand jury proceedings.<b> </b>The<b> </b>judge initially<b> </b>decided<b> </b>there was no longer a need to review them because<b> </b>prosecutors<b> </b>dropped<b> </b>the<b> </b>grand<b> </b>jury’s<b> </b>indictment.<br><br><b>May 21: </b>Having finally reviewed the unredacted grand jury transcripts at the urging of defense attorneys, Perry<b> </b>reveals<b> </b>that she was “incredibly shocked”<b> </b>to find that they documented<b> </b>alleged misconduct<b> </b>by Boutros’ staff. Boutros appears in court to<b> </b>personally<b> </b>drop the charges against the remaining<b> </b>four<b> </b>members of the “Broadview Six.”<b> </b>Boutros also assures<b> </b>Perry<b> </b>that<b> </b>he<b> </b>didn’t know about certain<b> </b>misconduct<b> </b>by his staff until<b> </b>late<b> </b>April<b> </b>2026.<br><br><b>July 1-2: </b>News breaks that Chicago FBI boss Douglas<b> </b>DePodesta<b> </b>would be leaving his job unexpectedly. An FBI social media account responds to news of his departure with the message, “Anyone who is not on board with THIS FBI under the leadership of President Trump … is free to leave.” Boutros tells reporters that DePodesta’s departure “was news to me.” DePodesta’s<b> </b>sister-in-law<b> </b>is a defense attorney<b> </b>representing<b> </b>a member of the “Broadview Six.”<br><br><b>July 9: </b>Following weeks of bad headlines generated by the “Broadview Six” controversy, Boutros<b> </b>is ordered into court<b> </b>by<b> </b>U.S. Magistrate Judge Laura<b> </b>McNally, who concludes that a secrecy order she’d entered<b> </b>in a separate case<b> </b>was violated<b> </b>by<b> </b>a<b> </b>Washington<b> </b>press conference Boutros participated in July 1 with then-Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche<b> </b>and FBI Director Kash Patel.<br><br><b>Aug. 4: </b>Boutros<b> </b>files a brief in the “Broadview Six” case acknowledging<b> </b>that, in<b> </b>October<b> </b>2025, he’d<b> </b>received<b> </b>by<b> </b>email<b> </b>a grand jury transcript that documented alleged wrongdoing by his staff — the same misconduct<b> </b>he’d<b> </b>told<b> </b>Perry<b> </b>he<b> </b>was<b> </b>unaware<b> </b>of<b> </b>until<b> </b>April. Boutros says he doesn’t remember reading it.<br><br><b>Nov. 2: </b>DePodesta<b> </b>sues<b> </b>Boutros, alleging Boutros<b> </b>falsely<b> </b>told his superiors<b> </b>that<b> </b>DePodesta and his sister-in-law conspired<b> </b>to<b> </b>destroy<b> </b>the<b> </b>“Broadview Six”<b> </b>case, and that DePodesta<b> </b>was eventually forced to resign. Separately, Perry<b> </b>issues<b> </b>a<b> </b>seven-page order finding<b> </b>that<b> </b>Boutros’ claims<b> </b>were<b> </b>“hard to credit”<b> </b>and<b> </b>“nearly unfathomable.”<b> </b>She<b> </b>orders<b> </b>Boutros<b> </b>and others to appear in court<b> </b>to testify<b> </b>about the “Broadview Six” case on<b> </b>Nov. 16.</div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: New Bears DT Jeffery Simmons' arrival at Halas Hall has been flawless, on and off the field
entries.summary: <p>Amid the whirlwind of getting traded — very abruptly — from the Titans to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons compartmentalized the upheaval and focused all his attention on preparing to debut on short notice against the Seahawks on Monday.</p><p>He asserted himself as a pseudo-captain from the jump, got the game plan mostly down and picked out a bright orange undershirt so his young daughter could find him on TV.</p><p>But he missed one crucial detail.</p><p>After <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/11/02/bears-big-plan-coming-together-beautifully-as-34-17-win-over-seahawks-pushes-them-to-best-start-since-2012" >the Bears’ 34-17 win in Seattle</a>, coach Ben Johnson gathered everyone in the visiting locker room at Lumen Field for his postgame recap, game balls and what has become his signature celebration, the stanky leg.</p><p>Simmons laughed at that last part, but when Johnson went into his, “Good, better, best,” chant, he was lost. Defensive end Montez Sweat, a college buddy of his from Mississippi State, tried to help him, but Simmons couldn’t catch up.</p><p>“I’ve definitely been on YouTube trying to figure that out and make sure I’m good for next game,” he said. “Next game, especially when I’m on camera like that, I’ll know the words. I’ll be ready.”</p><p>That aside, his arrival at Halas Hall has been flawless.</p><p>Simmons hasn’t needed any acclimation on or off the field. He was everything the Bears craved at the heart of their defense with six tackles, a sack and various assists to teammates Monday, and within a matter of days, he has established himself as a leader.</p><p>His résumé in that department is as impressive as the four Pro Bowl selections he earned on the grass. Simmons had an ideal mentor early in his career in former Bears safety Kevin Byard and became a Titans captain himself at just 24.</p><p>One of his passions outside football is fishing, which he learned from his grandfather while growing up in the tiny town of Macon, Miss., and he used it to bond with Titans teammates. And yes, he trash talks even while fishing.</p><p>When quarterback Cam Ward got drafted, Simmons took him out on the water, so as Bears quarterback Caleb Williams looks to connect with his new teammate, he might want to stop by Bass Pro Shops.</p><p>Williams said Wednesday he and Simmons hadn’t had much time to talk yet, but already something caught his attention. As players packed up the locker room at Lumen, Williams told teammates to tidy up and not leave a mess for staffers.</p><p>Simmons wasn’t around when he said that, but great minds think alike, and he went around the room picking up trash before he left.</p><p>“He's an All-Pro, he's a this and that; he could walk out, and nobody would say anything, [but] he's cleaning up the whole locker room, offensive and defensive side,” Williams said. “That's who he is. ... He's going to lead those guys and make those guys better.”</p><p>Simmons recognized quickly that the Bears, under Johnson, already have been winning and have an airtight culture, so his intent was essentially to fit into that framework.</p><p>He brought his own flair to it, starting Day 1 by challenging Sweat and defensive tackle Grady Jarrett to play better with him by their side, but in many ways, joining a team stacked with serious, veteran players was an environment he idealized and sought to foster with the Titans.</p><p>“I’m not trying to change anything that’s already been built around here,” Simmons said of the Bears. “How can I elevate that even more? That’s with my play, and off the field is where a lot of games are won. Things that we don’t think matter or may seem small at the time, that’s what helps good teams become great teams.”</p><p>He still has a lot to sort out — he’s living in a hotel and adjusting to calling his daughter on FaceTime instead of seeing her daily — and fortunately the Bears have a bye week after their game Sunday night against the Buccaneers. His family is coming to town for that game, his first at Soldier Field as a Bear, and then he has a window to return to Nashville before the Bears start practicing for their Nov. 22 game against the Saints.</p><p>It's a sharp turn for a player who had spent life exclusively in the South until last week and signed a three-year contract extension in June thinking he might play his entire career for the Titans. But as Simmons said, “Things change,” and he seems at home on the football field no matter where it is.</p>

entries.title: Previewing the best second-round IHSA football playoff games
entries.summary: <p>Here's a look at some of the best games in the second round of the IHSA playoffs. Check out all the pairings <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/scores/2026/10/17/high-school-football-ihsa-state-playoff-pairings-brackets-illinois-2026" >here</a>. </p><h3>Class 7A: No. 11 Batavia at No. 3 Brother Rice, 4 p.m. Saturday</h3><p>Two of the state's top quarterbacks match up here. Batavia senior Michael Vander Luitgaren, a Wyoming commit, has completed 73% of his passes for 2,638 yards and 30 touchdowns with six interceptions. He also leads the Bulldogs (8-2) in rushing with 714 yards and 15 TDs. Devin Ashiru is a rare 1,000-yard receiver with 85 catches for 1,068 yards and nine scores. Freshman Sam Holcomb is now the full-time starter for Rice (8-2) after splitting time earlier in the season. He's completing 74% of his passes for 1,320 yards and 21 TDs with no interceptions. Notre Dame recruit Brayden Parks and Kameron McGee lead a formidable defensive front for the Crusaders.</p><p></p><h3>Class 8A: No. 13 St. Ignatius at No. 8 Maine South, 2 p.m. Saturday</h3><p>St. Ignatius (8-2) is having a bounceback season after missing the IHSA playoffs the last two years. A big reason is the play of junior quarterback Reid Hites, who missed almost all of last season with an injury but now leads a potent option offense. Maine South (9-1) lost its opener to Batavia and has been tested only twice since, beating Central Suburban South rivals Glenbrook South and New Trier by a touchdown each. Indiana-bound quarterback Jameson Purcell has put up big numbers despite often not playing much in the second half. Last week against O'Fallon, he threw for 293 yards and four TDs in three quarters.</p><p></p><h3>Class 4A: No. 15 Montini at No 19 Morris, 4 p.m. Saturday</h3><p>The winner of this game becomes the favorite to win the 4A championship. Like most powerhouse teams this year, they each have an elite quarterback. Morris (1-0) is led by junior LaSalle-Peru transfer Marion Persich, who has completed 70% of his passes for 1,353 yards and 17 touchdowns with four interceptions while running for a team-high 933 yards and 19 TDs. Montini (8-2) counters with Miami commit Israel Abrams, a 64% passer for 2,471 yards and. 26 TDs. He also has 206 rushing yards and 14 TDs. Linebacker Ben Evenson had 101 tackles, including 15 for loss, to lead the Broncos defense.</p><p></p><h3>Class 5A: No. 17 Providence vs. No. 25 Morgan Park, noon Saturday at Stagg Stadium</h3><p>A week after coming from behind in the second half to eliminate a ranked Kankakee team, Providence (7-3) gets another tough test, It helps to have workhorse back Broden Mackert healthy. He ran for 241 yards and three touchdowns against the Kays and teams with running back/receiver Brayden McKay and quarterback Dominic Vita to lead a diverse offense. Morgan Park (9-1) has won nine straight since a five-point loss to Downers Grove North in Week 1 and is again the Public League's best team. Ole Miss commit Darrell Mattison can make an impact on both sides of the ball for the Mustangs and junior quarterback Ronald Smith Jr. has passed for 1,535 yards and 21 TDs with six interceptions.</p><p></p><h3>Class 8A: No. 12 Homewood-Flossmoor at No. 18 New Trier, 7 p.m. Friday</h3><p>Four-star defensive lineman David Hill, a Wisconsin commit, fuels a Homewood-Flossmoor defense that has four shutouts this season, including a 21-0 win against Conant last week. Junior quarterback Karter Nicholson threw for 187 yards and four TDs for the Vikings (8-2). New Trier (9-1) also has four shutouts and its only loss was by seven to Maine South. Purdue commit Jackie Ryder has thrown for 2,097 yards and 25 TDs. Junior Paul Liang is a player to watch as a receiver and punt returner.<br></p>

entries.title: Retiring fire commissioner grilled about 'downgrades' in emergency medical response
entries.summary: <p>Hours after a town house fire <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/11/05/4-killed-in-rogers-park-fire" >killed a family of four </a>in Rogers Park, questions about Chicago Fire Department equipment, training and paramedic shortages that "downgrade" the city's emergency response capability took center stage at City Hall.</p><p>Chicago Fire Department Commissioner Annette Nance-Holt wraps up a 37-year career May 26, when she hits the mandatory retirement age of 63. She was on the hot seat Thursday at what will be her final round of City Council budget hearings.</p><p>It started when Erik Steinmetz, president of Chicago Fire Fighters Union Local 2, complained about a shortage of ambulances, aging equipment and inadequate training that he said has led to Chicago having more line-of-duty deaths “than any other city in the country by far.”</p><p>“We don’t provide our firefighters with the continuing training they deserve, yet we expect them to confront some of the most dangerous environments imaginable. Too often, we have buried those very people we’ve asked to take those risks,” Steinmetz said.</p><p>The problems extend to emergency medical services, Steinmetz said, adding that Chicago “continues to downgrade advanced life support fire companies, taking paramedic level care out of our neighborhoods that depend on it."</p><p>Retiring 19th Ward Ald. Matt O’Shea, whose Far South Side ward is home to scores of firefighters and paramedics, then turned it up a notch.</p><p>He complained that the number of “advanced life support units downgraded” to basic-life support has “just exploded” in the past two weeks, slowing response times.</p><p>“I’m talking about people suffering cardiac arrest, an overdose, a stroke, a situation where minutes matter. We’re putting neighborhoods at risk,” O’Shea said. “We’re short paramedics. There’s an issue with paramedic pay. Nobody wants to be a medic. What are we doing to resolve this?”</p><p>Nance-Holt blamed a 2016 arbitration award that allowed firefighters to drop their paramedic license and downgrade to emergency medical technician.</p><p>“As a result, we’re experiencing shortages as far as firefighter/paramedics on [Advanced Life Support] engines and trucks,” she said.</p><p>“The answer is probably to sit down and talk about it again because my hands are tied with this… It’s not by our design to see this happen. .. There was a 10% increase for paramedics, crossovers in the budget. That still is not making people want to take those jobs. There is a shortage of paramedics in the whole country.”</p><p>When Ald. Gilbert Villegas (36th) probed more deeply into the shortage of paramedics, Nance-Holt talked about those who “choose to go elsewhere or work in suburban departments” where they can “make the same money or more” and not work nearly as hard racing from call to call.</p><p>Nance-Holt described the shortage of paramedics as “a national crisis,” adding, “Something happened after COVID where a lot of people just don’t consider that anymore.”</p><p>The shortage of paramedics reached a recent peak on Halloween night, when 17 of 90 fire trucks were “downgraded.”</p><p>“Sometimes, people choose not to work on those days. We can’t control that on ALS engines and trucks,” Nance-Holt said.</p><p>District Chief Mike Divita said it’s “hard to staff engines and trucks” on weekends and, since Halloween fell on a Saturday this year, the number of downgrades skyrocketed.</p><p>Overtime was offered “forwards and backwards” to the paramedics available “and we just didn’t have any takers. So we have come up with a list that we can strategically downgrade fire companies.”</p><p>Nance-Holt said “nobody wants to downgrade. That just sounds really bad.” But she is “faced with a lot of different obstacles” that require it, including more firefighters seeking “work/life balance” and taking advantage of family and parental leave.</p><p>“They have to… figure out how to work through this. It needs to be dealt with,” Nance-Holt said.</p><p>Steinmetz said the 3.5% pay differential between EMTs and paramedics — $30 a paycheck — is nowhere near enough to justify the heavy workload and massive liability.</p><p>In Seattle, paramedics make 17% more than EMTs. In Los Angeles, it’s 10%.</p><p>“Ten percent [differential] would bring some of the people back. Fifteen percent would probably get just about everybody back," he said.</p><p>The perennial problem of aging fire rigs — with 48% of fire engines and 38% of fire trucks over 15 years old — is expected to be remedied by a multi-year purchase, though it will take time to deliver new vehicles.</p><p>Still reeling from the "tragic loss of life" in her Rogers Park ward, Ald. Maria Hadden (49th) had only praise for the firefighters who tried to save her four constituents. </p><p>"I know that these are the types of tragedies that you all deal with on a daily basis multiple times a day," Hadden said.</p>
entries.author: Fran Spielman

entries.title: OK, Miami is No. 1 and Notre Dame No. 11, but who's actually better? College football Week 10 picks
entries.summary: <p>Man, oh, man, does the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports" target="_blank" >College Football Playoff</a> committee ever love it some SEC.</p><p>That was the biggest takeaway from <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports/2026/11/03/cfp-rankings-miami-indiana-notre-dame-college-football" target="_blank" >this season’s initial playoff rankings</a>, released Tuesday. Seven SEC teams packed the top 14 spots, and — more to the point — every SEC team with a pulse was ranked higher by the committee than it was in the AP and coaches’ polls.</p><p>Good for the SEC. Its feelings were hurt after the Big Ten won back-to-back-to-back national championships, but now it can feel special again.</p><p>What else about the CFP rankings stands out? Here’s one huge thing: the 10-spot gap between the top team, unbeaten ACC powerhouse Miami, and one-loss Notre Dame.</p><p>Do the 8-0 Hurricanes deserve to be No. 1? Sure, that’s fine. But with the Fighting Irish at 11, they’re right back where they were a year ago, only this time it’s plain and obvious — they can’t lose a second game, to Miami or anybody else, and expect to make the 12-team playoff field.</p><p>That makes the highest-profile game in a sparkling Week 10 lineup — <b>No. 1 Miami (+7½) at No. 11 Notre Dame </b>(6:30 p.m., NBC 5, 780-AM)<b> </b>—<b> </b>an absolute must-win for the Irish.</p><p>The huge point spread, with the Irish favored by more than a touchdown, merely suggests the committee isn’t seeing what oddsmakers and bettors are seeing: that the Irish pretty clearly are one of the best teams out there. This is the first time a No. 1 team in the playoff rankings has ever been an underdog against an opponent not in the top 10.</p><p>Last season, the Irish lost 27-24 at Miami, a result that came back to haunt them when the playoff bracket was finalized. Both teams might be better a year later.</p><p>The Hurricanes have upgraded at quarterback — Darian Mensah is one great night from grabbing control of the Heisman Trophy race — but they’re without Malachi Toney, one of the most explosive offensive playmakers in the country, who had ankle surgery this week. Mensah still has plenty of weapons to work with, including his own two legs. The Irish will have to keep him from controlling third downs with sprints for the sticks. Not having Toney will show up and hurt Miami at some point.</p><p>Irish win, 27-23, and move into next week’s top six.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/college-sports/2026/11/03/cfp-rankings-miami-indiana-notre-dame-college-football" target="_blank" >Miami is No. 1 in first CFP rankings; Indiana is fourth with Notre Dame at No. 11</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p><h3><b>Other Week 10 picks</b></h3><p><i>All games are Saturday unless otherwise noted. My picks to cover are listed first, with CFP rankings in effect.</i></p><p><b>Illinois (+4½) vs. Nebraska </b>(7 p.m. Friday, Fox 32, 890-AM): Statistically, the Huskers are better. On Planet Reality, they’ve lost three straight games, continue to falter uncannily in tight finishes and are 10 years removed from their last winning season in the Big Ten. Illini walk it off with a field goal.</p><p><b>No. 3 Utah (-4½) vs. No. 9 BYU </b>(11 a.m., ABC 7): BYU has scrapped its way to victory in three straight Holy War games. Utes end the streak — 24-16 — by running the ball and then running it some more.</p><p><b>No. 5 Alabama (+6½) at No. 14 LSU </b>(2:30 p.m., ABC 7): This will be the rivals’ 20th meeting since the last time LSU beat Alabama by a wide enough margin to cover this spread. That’s a trend I can’t ignore. LSU wins, though, 27-24.</p><p><b>No. 12 Ohio State (-7½) vs. No. 23 Oregon </b>(2:30 p.m., CBS 2): Buckeyes QB Luke Fahey wasn’t bad in a loss at USC, his first start, and the freshman should be a lot more comfortable back at home. Time for the Buckeyes to rise up on the other side of the ball, too. They get it done, 23-10.</p><p><b>No. 13 Tennessee (-6½) vs. No. 6 Kentucky </b>(5:15 p.m., ESPN): To say Tennessee has owned this rivalry is an understatement. Does that offset the fact the surprising Wildcats have won on the road against Texas A&M, South Carolina and Oklahoma? The Vols’ sack-happy D might be the difference. Vols, 30-21.</p><p><b>Northwestern (-2½) vs. No. 19 Iowa </b>(6:30 p.m., Fox 32, 720-AM): Wildcats QB Aidan Chiles has been so good. Hawkeyes fans will be everywhere at the new Ryan Field, but this might be Chiles’ moment. Cats, 23-20.</p><p>My favorite favorite: <b>No. 2 Georgia (-3½) at No. 10 Ole Miss </b>(6:30 p.m., ABC 7): The real No. 1 team in the country? It’s the Bulldogs. At least, I’m riding with them to win the natty if I have to pick a team today.</p><p>My favorite underdog: <b>No. 18 Missouri (+2½) vs. No. 7 Texas </b>(11 a.m., ESPN): The Tigers are too physical up front on defense, and the Longhorns have too many injury concerns. Upset.</p><p><b>Last week: </b>5-3 straight-up, 6-2 against the spread.</p><p><b>Season to date: </b>46-18 straight-up, 37-27 against the spread.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/UE9mQit9Phw?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="Spotlighitng Aidan Chiles | Northwestern Football | The Journey"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p></p>

entries.title: Remote patrol: NBC has best college football duo on best game of the year
entries.summary: <p>It has been 38 years since Notre Dame, then ranked No. 4, beat top-ranked Miami in South Bend in the famous “Catholics vs. Convicts” game, an all-time clash in college football history.</p><p>The longtime rivals will reprise that meeting Saturday, with No. 1 Miami visiting No. 11 Notre Dame (6:30 p.m., NBC 5, 780-AM). NBC will give it big-game treatment with an expanded pregame show and a sideline reporter for each team.</p><p>But where NBC differentiates itself is in the booth, where <b>Noah Eagle</b> and <b>Todd Blackledge</b> form the best TV duo in college football, despite their 36-year age gap (Eagle is 29, Blackledge is 65). In fact, it’s believed to be the biggest between regular partners in major sports.</p><p>It hasn’t hurt them one bit. Eagle likely has learned from his father, <b>Ian</b>, who has called basketball with <b>Bill Rafter</b>y for decades, defying their 25-year gap. Eagle and Blackledge work great together and sound more like they’re contemporaries than from different generations.</p><h3>White Sox ratings</h3><p>The Sox’ stunning season meant huge ratings for Chicago Sports Network, another reflection of how the team captured fans’ attention.</p><p>On CHSN’s linear and streaming platforms, Sox games averaged 84,800 viewers per game, a major-league best 168% increase from last year and the team’s biggest audience since 2022. That audience grew throughout the season, with games in August and September averaging 112,000 viewers, a 78% increase from March, April and May.</p><p>The 2022 season followed a playoff season. Barring a lockout, another increase could be in the offing. With the Bulls and Blackhawks struggling, CHSN really needs a baseball season.</p><h3>They said it</h3><p><b>Bob Costas</b> admirably continues to support late Cubs radio voice <b>Jack Quinlan</b>, who died in 1965, for the Hall of Fame. He told WGN Radio's <b>Bob Sirott</b> on Thursday that he's more optimistic than ever because the electorate has Quinlan's work: "All you have to do is listen to those tapes to see that if you confined it to the dozen best baseball broadcasters of all time, he was actually one of them."</p><p>• “NHL on TNT” <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/04/blackhawks-panthers-tnt-paul-bissonnette-connor-bedard" >studio analyst <b>Paul Bissonnette</b></a> had lots of company tearing into the Blackhawks on Wednesday. <b>Jay Zawaski</b> took his turn on CHGO’s postgame show: “You heard <b>Jeff Blashill</b> say after the Avalanche game, ‘Well, when you take the emotions of the score out of it, it was actually a really good game.’ F that. You suck. You're the worst team in hockey.”</p><p>• The Score's <b>Mark Grote</b> made me laugh Wednesday when he said it was time to forgive former Bears quarterbacks, now that the team has <b>Caleb Williams</b>: "The sentence is not over for <b>Cody Parkey</b> right now. But I believe the sentence is over for <b>Mitch Trubisky</b>, and maybe even <b>Todd Collins</b> and <b>Caleb Hanie</b> and <b>Chad Hutchinson</b>. Somebody stop me, please!"</p>
entries.author: Jeff Agrest

entries.title: NFL primetime TV rankings: Bears cap three-game run with best of the bunch
entries.summary: <p>We’re almost there. The stretch of three consecutive primetime regular-season Bears games — a first for the team since at least 2000 — will end Sunday with a home game against the Buccaneers. Deadline-driven writers and editors, rejoice!</p><p>After a bye week, our lives will return to some normalcy with three of the next four games scheduled to kick off at noon on Sundays, and none figure to be flexed. The other will kick off at noon on Thanksgiving.</p><p>This three-week run has given us the chance to hear the announcing teams for the NFL’s three primetime partners — Prime Video, ESPN and NBC — broadcast the Bears. That got me thinking: How should they be ranked?</p><p>We love to rank things here (our seventh annual Chicago sports-media power rankings are only three months away), so why not these guys? And fortunately for Bears fans, the NFL saved the best for last.</p><h3><b>1. Mike Tirico & Cris Collinsworth, NBC’s “Sunday Night Football”</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Tirico is the best play-by-play broadcaster in the business. He’s one of the few national announcers who sounds like he has been calling your team’s games for years. His ability to absorb tons of information and recall it at the perfect time is uncanny.</p><p>For TV, his amount of play-by-play is just right, and he can make it memorable, like he did when Caleb Williams connected with Cole Kmet in the final half-minute of the playoff game against the Rams: “They’ve done it again! Unbelievable! … I don’t believe this team.” Perhaps he’ll have another in store for the game Sunday against the Buccaneers.</p><p>Reviews of Collinsworth run the gamut — did you know there’s an “I hate Cris Collinsworth” Facebook page? — but I enjoy him. His football IQ is off the charts, he has a great rapport with Tirico and he’s good for a one-liner now and then. Dare I bring up “double doink”? Sorry.</p><h3><b>2. Joe Buck & Troy Aikman, ESPN’s “Monday Night Football”</b></h3><h3></h3><p>These two have been in the news a lot lately because they’re on the outs after 25 years. ESPN gave Buck a new contract but not Aikman, and the situation came to a head with a verbal confrontation in the booth before a game last month. Aikman later said he’ll be a free agent after the season, which ESPN will cap with its first Super Bowl. Should be quite a run-up.</p><p>Whatever the reasons for their impending divorce, Buck and Aikman continue to put on a professional broadcast. They even seemed to like each other during the Bears-Seahawks game. Buck always has been solid, and Aikman has strong opinions.</p><p>That said, I don’t always like Buck’s staccato calls, and Aikman can sound holier than thou. Other than those quibbles, they’ve stabilized a once-turbulent booth — until Aikman leaves, that is.</p><h3><b>3. Al Michaels & Kirk Herbstreit, Prime Video’s “Thursday Night Football”</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Michaels is the greatest play-by-play announcer of all time, but that time is not now. Though his voice brings gravitas to a broadcast, he’s slower on the draw and short on emotion. It’s uncertain whether Michaels, 81, will return next season.</p><p>As for Herbstreit, it always has felt like he drops in to call an NFL game amid all of his college football work, which includes “College GameDay” and ESPN’s top game of the week. How can he not be spread too thin? Sometimes it sounds that way.</p><p>The two don’t exactly click, either. What saves the broadcast is Prime’s outstanding production, from video quality to innovative graphic elements. Plus, you can buy stuff!</p>
